title: Finance (Income Taxes) Bill 2026 passed by Parliament — MMTA amendments incl. GIR exchange framework
summary: Bill 22/2026 passed 6 Oct; still needs presidential assent and gazetting. MMTA changes: Side-by-Side safe harbour from 1 Jan 2026 (MTT relief for qualifying US-parented groups; DTT unaffected); GIR exchange framework with a local fallback filing where a centrally filed GIR is not received; Ministerial power to exempt MTT/DTT returns; regulation power to use statutory financial statements as FANIL for DTT. ITA side gives effect to Budget 2026 measures incl. YA2026 CIT rebate.
relevance_action: SbS is irrelevant to Razer because the group is SG-parented, not US-parented. What matters: (1) as UPE jurisdiction, SG's GIR exchange framework is the legal basis for Razer's central GIR filing to reach AU/ID/JP/MY/IN, so confirm the exchange relationships are active for each; (2) assess whether a local-statutory-accounts FANIL election for DTT reduces adjustments for the SG CEs once regs issue; (3) monitor eGazette for assent and book the YA2026 rebate in provisions.
source: oecdpillars.com (passage); SG Government Gazette Bills Supplement No. 22 (introduction)
trust_note: Passage confirmed only by a secondary tracker. Verify on parliament.gov.sg / sso.gov.sg.

title: IRAS publishes list of Qualified Tax Incentives for Substance-based Tax Incentive (SbTI) safe harbour
summary: IRAS updated its Pillar Two guidance to identify which SG incentives and components qualify for the SbTI safe harbour under DTT, distinguishing specified base vs enhanced deductions. The safe harbour is elective and capped by a substance cap.
relevance_action: Map every incentive or enhanced deduction claimed by the SG CEs against the QTI list. Then model the SbTI election for FY2026 SG ETR/DTT, testing the cap against SG payroll and tangible assets (likely thin for a services/payments footprint).

title: Budget 2027 tabled — standard CIT unchanged; GSH 5% rate; new salary-deduction condition for non-SMEs
summary: 24% headline rate unchanged; SME rates cut to 14%/16%. Enhanced Global Services Hub incentive from 1 Jan 2027: 5% rate, up to 30 years, WHT exemption on interest and stamp duty exemption on interco loans for treasury activities. Small-value asset threshold raised to RM3,000 per asset (RM30,000 overall cap for non-MSMEs). New conditions for non-SME companies to deduct salary costs from YA2028.
relevance_action: RMS Reloads is a non-SME (group-level), so 24% applies; base CP204 for YA2027 on that. RISK FLAG on GSH: with MY's QDMTT in force, a 5% hub rate for an in-scope group is largely topped back up to 15% domestically unless it qualifies as a QTI. Do not treat the GSH as a group ETR saving. Watch the Finance Bill for the YA2028 salary-deduction conditions, which are a payroll compliance gating risk.

title: 57th GST Council — export-of-services reforms, place-of-supply change, decriminalisation
summary: Recommendations: omit IGST s.2(6)(v), so supplies to an overseas establishment of a distinct person can qualify as exports; omit s.13(3)(a), so the default recipient-location rule applies; circular on receipt of consideration in FX/INR; ITC refund on input services under inverted duty from 1 Nov 2026; removal of s.69 arrest powers; prosecution threshold raised ₹1cr→₹5cr. No rate changes. All require CGST/IGST amendments and notifications.
relevance_action: No OIDAR-specific change surfaced, so the OIDAR position stands. Ask Deloitte whether any of RO Pvt Ltd's cross-border services to SG group entities were at risk under s.13(3)(a) or the FX-receipt condition, and whether the changes open refund claims. Track the enabling amendments.

title: PMK 71/2026 — tax debt payments applied to principal first; objection/sanction procedures refined
summary: In force 2 Oct (DGT statement 12 Oct). Payments now settle principal tax debt first rather than pro-rata against principal and sanctions. The PMK also refines timelines for responding to audit-result findings and clarifies reduction or elimination of administrative sanctions.
relevance_action: If any SKP/STP is outstanding or under dispute, re-plan payments so principal clears first and the sanction-waiver route stays open. Recheck internal deadlines for audit-finding responses against the revised timelines.
trust_note: Pull the PMK text from JDIH Kemenkeu before acting.

title: Draft decree implementing Resolution 43/2026/QH16 — 30% CIT reduction (FY2026–27) for revenue ≤ VND 10bn
summary: MoF was required to submit the decree by 10 Oct. Under the draft, qualifying enterprises self-apply the 30% reduction in quarterly provisional CIT. The reduction is computed after existing incentives, and there is an anti-fragmentation rule for post-resolution splits. Promulgation not yet confirmed.
relevance_action: THS is likely out of scope if its revenue exceeds VND 10bn; confirm with BDO and close. If in scope, apply from the next quarterly provisional payment.

title: No new OECD release in window; jurisdictions legislating Jan 2026 package (TCSH extension, SbS)
summary: France tabled an amendment (10 Oct) for SbS/UPE safe harbours and a one-year Transitional CbCR Safe Harbour extension. Sweden submitted a bill (13 Oct) extending the TCSH to FYs beginning before 1 Jan 2028. OECD has signalled further guidance on other potentially discriminatory tax features before end-2026.
relevance_action: Watch only. Confirm the TCSH extension is enacted in every Razer CE jurisdiction before relying on it for FY2027. Monitor the year-end OECD guidance on discriminatory taxes for QDMTT-qualification knock-ons in ID/MY/JP/AU/VN.
